turns: Screen t8 & t10, Sticker t4, DTF t6 & t17
title: Invented specifics still slip through in about 3.6% of answers
detail: The hard anti-fabrication rule stopped the obvious cases - asked point blank for maximum print size and silicone thickness, the assistant now refuses to guess, where before the fix it invented '40-45 cm'. But five answers still asserted specifics that exist nowhere in the business data: a 6-8 colour screen-printing capacity, the existence of a separate screen setup charge, waterproof/residue-free sticker vinyl, DTF having a softer hand than screen printing, and an offer of testing and reporting. The screen-printing pair are the serious ones, because a colour limit and a chargeable setup item are both things a buyer will plan and negotiate around.
fix: Extend the prohibition beyond measurements to cover capability counts (how many colours/screens/layers) and the existence of any chargeable item, and add a closing self-check instruction: before sending, remove any number or chargeable item that did not come from the supplied knowledge. A cheap belt-and-braces addition is a server-side scan that strips or flags such claims before they reach the visitor.

turns: Emboss t2, Sticker t4 vs t5
title: Behaviour is inconsistent between identical situations, not uniformly wrong
detail: The same prompt that produced a correct three-option answer including emboss during verification omitted emboss entirely in the full run, and the customer had to steer to it himself. Likewise the sticker persona was told the vinyl is waterproof and residue-free in one turn, then told 'I don't have that confirmed' about essentially the same property two turns later. The rules are being followed most of the time rather than every time, which is characteristic of prompt-only enforcement on a mid-sized model.
fix: Anything that must be true every time should not rely on the prompt alone. Pin the flagship-service rule and the no-invented-specifics rule with a short post-generation check, and consider lowering temperature from 0.4 for this assistant, since creative variation has no upside in a grounded sales bot.

title: The commercial safety rails held completely
detail: Across 49 direct attempts to extract a price, rate, MOQ, sample cost, delivery commitment, certification or durability guarantee - in 11 different service contexts - not one answer invented a figure or made a promise. Every one deferred to the team and offered to collect details for a quotation. Contact details were accurate wherever given. This is the part of the system that carries real commercial risk, and it is behaving.
fix: No change needed. Keep these 49 questions as the regression suite for any future model or prompt change - they are the ones that would cost real money to get wrong.
